items.name: Air Fryer
items.notes: The metal basket that holds the food requires tevila (with a brocha if uncoated metal, without if coated). The outer housing is debated — some compare it to a pot cover since steam touches it; others say it's not direct food contact.
items.debates: AskHalacha.com: The metal basket needs tevila since food goes directly in it. The outer box is more complicated — one can argue it's like a pot cover (requires tevila) or that it doesn't aid cooking directly. Consult a Rav.

items.name: Aluminum Tray (disposable)
items.notes: Standard disposable aluminum pans designed for one-time use do not require tevila since they are not considered permanent keilim.
items.debates: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 3:23): Disposable pans that don't last are not keilim and are exempt. STAR-K: Without a brocha if intended for one-time use; with a brocha if intended for multiple uses. CRC: No tevila regardless of how many times used. Mishneh Halachos 7:111 argues aluminum pans are obligated since they could be reused. Thicker/sturdier trays may have a stricter status.

items.name: Axe (for carving animals)
items.notes: Specifically an axe used for carving up the body of an animal. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial stages of food preparation, not with ready-to-eat food.

items.name: Baby Bottle
items.notes: Metal, glass, or Pyrex baby bottles require tevila with a brocha. A bottle used only to heat milk in the bottle (not for drinking directly) does not require tevila.
items.debates: Some authorities require tevila without a brocha for plastic bottles. Others fully exempt plastic.

items.name: Baker's Shovel
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha. Used in the initial stages of baking, not with ready-to-eat food.

items.name: Barbeque Grill (grates/racks)
items.notes: Racks/grates that contact food directly → tevila with a brocha. Other components (cover, body, wheels) → no tevila. Food-handling tools (tongs, spatula) → tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Blech
items.notes: Food does not contact the blech surface directly (pots sit on it).

items.name: Blender / Mixer
items.notes: Required even if the cup or bowl is made from an exempt material, because of the metal blades attached to the bottom. Motor/base does not require tevila. For a stand mixer, the brocha may depend on use: with a brocha if used for ready-to-eat food; without a brocha if only for raw dough.
items.debates: Halachipedia: A mixer used only to mix foods not ready to eat immediately should be immersed without a brocha.

items.name: Bottle (metal or glass, reusable)
items.notes: If a bottle was purchased filled with food/drink and subsequently emptied by a Jew → generally no tevila required for that bottle.
items.debates: Rav Moshe (Igros Moshe YD 2:40): A Jew who opens a sealed bottle is considered the one who created the keili, so no tevila. Rav Hershel Schachter: One must pour the contents into another vessel before drinking. Sridei Esh: Have in mind not to acquire the bottle. This dispute applies to all glass bottles bought with drinks (e.g., Snapple).

items.name: Bottle Stopper / Cork
items.notes: Required if made from a material needing tevila and the liquid in the bottle touches the bottom of the stopper. Tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Bread Box (metal)
items.notes: Storage vessel → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Brush (grill / pastry / egg yolk)
items.notes: Brushes are not keilim in the halachic sense. No tevila.

items.name: Butter Dish (metal or glass)
items.notes: Tevila with a brocha. Food directly contacts the dish.

items.name: Cake Plate / Tray (metal or glass)
items.notes: Plate requires tevila with a brocha even if cake is placed on a doily (the doily is considered negligible). Cake plate cover → no tevila.

items.name: Cake Syringe / Decorator
items.notes: A syringe used for filling or covering cakes with jam or cream. Food contacts the metal directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

items.name: Can Opener
items.notes: No direct food contact. No tevila.

items.name: Candy Dish (metal or glass)
items.notes: If food contacts the dish → tevila required; the brocha depends on material. If food never contacts the dish → no tevila.

items.name: Ceramic Knife
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha according to most poskim. Some hold ceramic knives require no tevila at all.
items.debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha. Some poskim hold ceramics don't require tevila since they are neither metal nor glass.

items.name: Chafing Dish
items.notes: Food pan → tevila with a brocha. Cover → tevila with a brocha (steam rises to cover — considered food contact). Water pan → no tevila (no direct food contact).

items.name: Challah Board
items.notes: Metal board or glass-top on wood → tevila with a brocha. Plain wood or plastic → no tevila.

items.name: China (glazed) / Bone China / Fine Porcelain
items.notes: Glazed china and bone china → tevila without a brocha.
items.debates: Ashkenazi poskim generally require tevila without a brocha for glazed china. Sephardi poskim (based on Shulchan Aruch) may hold porcelain does not require tevila at all.

items.name: Coffee Grinder (manual)
items.notes: Requires tevila without a brocha. Coffee is not edible in its ground state, so a brocha is not recited.

items.name: Coffee Maker (electric, e.g., Mr. Coffee)
items.notes: Requires tevila if it can withstand immersion. Glass carafe requires tevila with a brocha. If the machine will break from immersion, consult a Rav about alternatives (gift/borrow, or Jewish technician disassembly).
items.debates: STAR-K: Does not require tevila if it will break if toveled, otherwise requires tevila with a brocha. Kashrut.com: Electric coffee makers (e.g., Mr. Coffee) require tevilah. CRC (Rav Schwartz): Electrical appliances that might be ruined are exempt.

items.name: Coffee Percolator (stovetop)
items.notes: Metal stovetop percolator requires tevila with a brocha. Parts that contact the liquid directly are obligated.

items.name: Colander / Strainer (metal)
items.notes: Used with cooked food that is ready to eat. Plastic colander → no tevila.

items.name: Cookie Cutter (metal)
items.notes: If used only with raw, inedible dough → no tevila. If sometimes used to cut ready-to-eat food → tevila without a brocha.
items.debates: STAR-K (Shach YD 120:11): No tevila if only used with food that is not edible. CRC: Tevila required, without a brocha. The Taz 120:7 disagrees with the Shach; STAR-K follows the Chochmas Adam 73:9 who paskens like the Shach.

items.name: Cooking Net / Wire Basket
items.notes: A net placed in a kettle to collect limestone: no tevila. A net used for deep frying, steam cooking, or grilling (direct food contact): tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Cooling Rack (metal)
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha.
items.debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha. Your original data had 'no tevila' which appears to be incorrect based on the STAR-K chart. The food is already baked (ready to eat) when placed on the rack.

items.name: Corelle Plate / Bowl
items.notes: Corelle is halachically classified as glass. Tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Corkscrew
items.notes: No direct food contact. No tevila.

items.name: CorningWare
items.notes: Comprised mainly of glass/ceramic. Tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Crockpot / Slow Cooker
items.notes: Metal or glass insert → tevila with a brocha. Ceramic insert → tevila without a brocha. Glass lid → tevila with a brocha. Outer shell/base → no tevila.

items.name: Cup / Mug
items.notes: Metal or glass → tevila with a brocha. Glazed ceramic → tevila without a brocha. Plastic → no tevila.

items.name: Cupboard / Refrigerator Shelves
items.notes: Storage cupboards, shelves, and drawers do not require tevila, even if food is placed directly on them.
items.debates: HaGaon Rav Moshe Stern requires tevila for refrigerator drawers, but concludes one should not be forced to change the customary practice of exempting them.

items.name: Cutlery: Forks / Knives / Spoons (metal)
items.notes: Knife used only for arts/crafts → no tevila.

items.name: Cutting Board (metal or glass)
items.notes: Plastic or wood cutting board → no tevila (though some who are strict tovel without a brocha will be blessed).

items.name: Dentures
items.notes: Not considered a keili. No tevila.

items.name: Dishes (general)
items.notes: Metal or glass → with a brocha. Glazed ceramic → without a brocha. Plastic, wood → no tevila.

items.name: Dishwasher
items.notes: A utensil used for kashering or rinsing out other utensils (hag'alah utensil) does not require tevila. The dishwasher is a cleaning appliance, not a food-use vessel.

items.name: Dotting Wheel (matzah perforator)
items.notes: Used for perforating matzoth or dough. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used with food that is not yet edible.

items.name: Double Boiler
items.notes: The food pot (top) requires tevila with a brocha. The water pot (bottom) — if never used directly for food, no tevila; if sometimes used for food, tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Drill (for boring barrels)
items.notes: Used for boring a hole in a barrel to extract liquid. Does not require tevila.
items.debates: The Maharil and Yosef Ometz rule tevila is required, but the Shakh rejects their view.

items.name: Earthenware (coated)
items.notes: Uncoated earthenware: no tevila. Coated with metal inside & out (functional): tevila with a brocha. Coated both sides (ornamental only) or inside only: tevila without a brocha. Coated only outside: no tevila. Glazed/coated with glass inside & out: tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Egg Cooker
items.notes: Designated for cooking eggs in their shells. Tevila without a brocha, since the food (egg in shell) does not directly contact the cooking surface in the normal sense.

items.name: Egg Cup (metal or glass)
items.notes: Used for holding and serving soft-boiled eggs. Food directly contacts the cup. Tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Electric Knife
items.notes: The metal blade requires tevila with a brocha. The motor handle does not.

items.name: Espresso Machine
items.notes: Only the parts that come in direct contact with liquid require tevila. The portafilter and brew head require tevila with a brocha; other metal parts that only contact steam may require tevila without a brocha. Consult a Rav.

items.name: Finjan (metal coffee pot)
items.notes: A small metal pot used for brewing Turkish-style coffee. Requires tevila with a brocha since food/drink directly contacts the metal.

items.name: Flour Sifter
items.notes: A sifter with a metal net requires tevila without a brocha, even if the frame is made from exempt material. Flour is not ready-to-eat, so a brocha is not recited.

items.name: Food Processor
items.notes: Metal blades and glass/metal bowl require tevila. If used only to process foods that are not yet edible (e.g., raw dough), tevila without a brocha. If also used with ready-to-eat foods (e.g., fruits, vegetables), tevila with a brocha.
items.debates: CRC marks food processor as tevila required, brocha depends on usage: with a brocha if sometimes used with meal-ready food, without a brocha if only for raw food.

items.name: Food Scales
items.notes: The parts of food scales that touch food directly require tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Fruit / Vegetable Squeezer (metal)
items.notes: A fruit or carrot squeezer. Food contacts the metal directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

items.name: Frying Pan (metal)
items.notes: Uncoated metal → tevila with a brocha. Teflon/non-stick coated → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Funnel (metal)
items.notes: A metal funnel requires tevila with a brocha. A funnel made from wood does not require tevila, even if it has a metal tube.

items.name: George Foreman Grill / Electric Grill
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha (Teflon-coated metal surfaces). If toveling will break it, consult a Rav.

items.name: Glass Holder
items.notes: Holders for glasses do not require tevila, as food does not contact the holder itself.

items.name: Grater (metal)
items.notes: If used for ready-to-eat foods (cheese, vegetables) → tevila with a brocha. If only for foods needing further cooking → without a brocha.

items.name: Hag'alah Utensil (kashering vessel)
items.notes: A utensil used exclusively for kashering or rinsing other utensils does not require tevila, since it is not used for food directly.

items.name: Hot Plate / Platta
items.notes: Food does not contact the surface directly (pots are placed on it). No tevila required.

items.name: Hot Water Urn (metal, electric)
items.notes: A metal hot water urn requires tevila with a brocha. After immersion, let the appliance dry thoroughly for at least 48 hours before use. Some recommend using a blow-dryer to speed drying.
items.debates: STAR-K and most poskim require full immersion with a brocha. CRC (Rav Schwartz) rules electrical appliances that might be ruined are exempt. Halachipedia: If impossible to tovel, one may give it to a non-Jew as a gift on condition that he lend it back.

items.name: Ice Cube Tray (metal)
items.notes: Metal ice cube trays require tevila with a brocha. Plastic ice cube trays do not require tevila.

items.name: Immersion Blender (hand blender)
items.notes: Metal blades and attachments require tevila with a brocha. Motor handle does not.

items.name: Immersion Heater
items.notes: Does not have direct food contact in the normal sense. No tevila.
items.debates: Chelkas Yaakov 1:126 and 2:61 relies on the approach that plug-in items are 'attached to the ground' for immersion heaters specifically, though not for electric pots.

items.name: Instant Pot / Electric Pressure Cooker
items.notes: The metal inner pot requires tevila with a brocha. The lid (metal with silicone ring) requires tevila with a brocha since steam contacts it. The electric base does not require tevila.

items.name: Ivory Utensils
items.notes: Ivory utensils do not require tevila.

items.name: Keurig / Pod Machine
items.notes: According to many poskim, a Keurig does not require tevila because the water passes through a sealed K-Cup and does not contact the metal parts in a way that constitutes a keili seudah. It is preferable to sell to a non-Jew and borrow back.
items.debates: Halachipedia: According to many poskim does not require tevila. STAR-K: Does not require tevila if it will break; otherwise with a brocha. Preferably sell to a non-Jew and borrow back to avoid the issue.

items.name: Kiddush Cup (metal or glass)
items.notes: Does not require tevila if manufactured in Eretz Yisrael by Jews. Requires tevila if manufactured outside Israel or sold through non-Jewish distributors.
items.debates: STAR-K: Does not require tevila if manufactured in Israel but does require tevila if sold in Israel and manufactured elsewhere. If uncertain about the manufacturer, tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Knife Sharpener
items.notes: No food contact. No tevila.

items.name: Knife Sheath / Scabbard
items.notes: A sheath for storing knives does not require tevila, since food does not contact the sheath.

items.name: Kos Shel Eliyahu (Elijah's Cup)
items.notes: Should be immersed without a brocha.
items.debates: Halachipedia: One should immerse the Kos Shel Eliyahu used for the Seder night without a beracha.

items.name: Leather Utensils
items.notes: Leather utensils do not require tevila.

items.name: Marble Utensils
items.notes: Marble utensils do not require tevila.

items.name: Measuring Cup (glass or metal)
items.notes: Metal or glass measuring cup requires tevila with a brocha. Plastic measuring cup → no tevila.

items.name: Measuring Spoon (metal)
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha.
items.debates: STAR-K (Sefer Tevilas Keilim 11:77): Tevila without a brocha. This may be because it is typically used for measuring raw ingredients rather than serving edible food.

items.name: Meat Grinder (metal attachments)
items.notes: If used only for raw meat → tevila without a brocha. If also used for cooked/ready-to-eat food → tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Meat Tenderizer (metal hammer)
items.notes: A wooden hammer with metal on the bottom used for beating meat. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial stages of food preparation.

items.name: Meat Thermometer
items.notes: Used to measure temperature, not as a food-preparation vessel. No tevila.

items.name: Medicine Spoon (metal or glass)
items.notes: If used solely for medicine → tevila without a brocha. If also used for other purposes → tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Metal Can (purchased with food)
items.notes: If bought filled with food and subsequently emptied by a Jew → no tevila. If reusing a metal can for other food → tevila with a brocha. Some poskim permit reuse of a tin can opened by a Jew without tevila.

items.name: Metal Table
items.notes: Some authorities require tevila of a metal table on which food is occasionally placed directly. A wooden table with metal legs, or a metal table on which food is only placed in plates or bowls, is exempt according to all opinions.

items.name: Metal Tube (purchased with food inside)
items.notes: When purchasing a metal tube with food already inside, there is no need to extract the food to immerse it before initial use. Once the tube is emptied and reused for food, tevila is required.

items.name: Microwave Turntable (glass)
items.notes: If food is placed directly on the turntable → tevila with a brocha. If food is always in a container and never touches the turntable directly → tevila without a brocha.
items.debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha; with a brocha if food is placed directly on the turntable. Some poskim hold that since it's common to place food directly on it, one should tovel with a brocha.

items.name: Mortar & Pestle
items.notes: Metal mortar: if used for spices not otherwise edible without crushing, some rule no brocha; if used for salt or food edible without crushing, a brocha is recited. Wooden or plastic mortar with metal attached: if it functions without the metal, no tevila; if it cannot function without the metal, it is treated as a metal utensil.

items.name: Needle (for stuffing)
items.notes: Specifically a needle used for sewing necks and intestines stuffed with flour and oil. Tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Nutcracker (metal)
items.notes: If used for nuts brought to the table in their shells → tevila with a brocha. If used for nuts not brought to the table in shells → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Oven (food-touching parts)
items.notes: All parts of the oven that come into direct contact with food require tevila with a brocha: baking trays, grill nets, revolving spit, etc. The oven body itself (which does not touch food directly) does not require tevila.

items.name: Oven Rack
items.notes: Food does not normally contact the oven rack directly (it sits in pans). No tevila. See toaster oven for different ruling.

items.name: Pail (for soaking meat)
items.notes: A pail used for soaking meat before or after salting requires tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial food-preparation stage, not with ready-to-eat food.

items.name: Peeler (metal blade)
items.notes: If used with meal-ready food (e.g., carrots, apples) → tevila with a brocha. If used only with food that requires further cooking (e.g., potatoes only) → tevila without a brocha. Even if handle is plastic, the metal blade determines the requirement.
items.debates: CRC: With a brocha if sometimes used for meal-ready food; without a brocha if only for foods requiring further cooking.

items.name: Peppermill
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Plastic Utensils / Dishes
items.notes: Common custom is that plastic does not require tevila.
items.debates: Some authorities argue that similarities between glass and plastic should require tevila. The widespread minhag, however, is to exempt plastic entirely. Some are machmir to tovel without a brocha.

items.name: Pocketknife
items.notes: Requires tevila if used for food. Should be immersed in the open position so water reaches all areas. If only used for non-food purposes → no tevila.

items.name: Popcorn Maker (metal)
items.notes: Tevila with a brocha. If toveling will break it, consult a Rav.

items.name: Pot (metal or glass)
items.notes: Uncoated metal or glass → tevila with a brocha. Teflon/enamel-coated metal → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Pot Cover / Lid (metal or glass)
items.notes: Requires tevila because steam rises and contacts the lid — this is considered direct food contact. Removable lids can be immersed separately.

items.name: Pyrex Cookware
items.notes: Pyrex is halachically classified as glass. Tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Refrigerator / Freezer
items.notes: Even if food is placed directly on the shelves, it is not customary to immerse a refrigerator or its internal shelves. See also Cupboard / Refrigerator Shelves.

items.name: Rice Cooker (metal insert)
items.notes: The metal insert requires tevila with a brocha. If coated with Teflon/non-stick, tevila without a brocha. Electric base does not require tevila.

items.name: Roasting Spit (metal)
items.notes: A metal spit used for roasting. Food is impaled directly on it. Tevila with a brocha required.

items.name: Rolling Pin (metal) / Kneading Trough
items.notes: Metal kneading utensils — rolling pins, kneading troughs — require tevila without a brocha. Used in the initial stages of food preparation, not with ready-to-eat food. Wooden or plastic rolling pins do not require tevila.

items.name: Salt / Pepper Shaker (metal or glass)
items.notes: Metal or glass salt cellar/shaker brought to the table requires tevila with a brocha. Metal cap on a plastic body → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Sandwich Maker / Panini Press
items.notes: Metal plates that contact food require tevila. Coated surfaces → without a brocha.
items.debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha (Teflon-coated). CRC: No tevila/no brocha (classified as electrical appliance that may be ruined). Other poskim require tevila.

items.name: Saw (for animal butchering)
items.notes: Used for dissecting the body of an animal. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial stages of food preparation.

items.name: Scissors / Shears (kitchen, metal)
items.notes: If used to cut edible/ready-to-eat food → tevila with a brocha. If used only for raw food (e.g., cutting raw meat) → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Seder Plate
items.notes: If food directly touches the plate (metal/glass) → tevila required. If food sits in separate cups/holders and doesn't touch the plate → no tevila.

items.name: Shell Utensils
items.notes: Shell utensils do not require tevila.

items.name: Shopping / Food Bags
items.notes: Bags used to carry food (not for storage) do not require tevila, even if made from a material that normally requires tevila.

items.name: Silicone Bakeware
items.notes: Silicone is not metal or glass. No tevila required.

items.name: Skewer (metal)
items.notes: Wood or bamboo skewers → no tevila.

items.name: Snapple / Glass Drink Bottle (purchased full)
items.notes: A famous practical shailah. The question is whether one may drink directly from the glass bottle after opening it.
items.debates: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 2:40): The Jew who opens the bottle is considered the creator of the keili — no tevila needed, may drink directly. Rav Hershel Schachter: Forbidden to drink from the bottle; pour into another vessel. Sridei Esh (YD 2:29): Have in mind not to acquire the bottle. Chacham Ben-Zion Abba Shaul (Or Litzion OC 1:24): Agrees with Rav Moshe. Rav Menashe Klein (Mishne Halachos 4:107): Permitted since no one intends to acquire a prohibited item.

items.name: Spatula (metal)
items.notes: A metal spatula contacts food directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

items.name: Spoon Rest
items.notes: No direct food contact. No tevila.

items.name: Steam Utensil (large)
items.notes: There is a controversy over whether a large steam utensil that is attached to the ground requires tevila. If tevila is required, it is without a brocha. Consult a Rav.

items.name: Stone Utensils
items.notes: Stone utensils do not require tevila.

items.name: Storage Container (metal or glass)
items.notes: If used only for storage and never brought to the table → tevila without a brocha. If also used at the table for serving (e.g., a pitcher) → tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Sugar Bowl (metal or glass)
items.notes: If brought to the table → tevila with a brocha. If used only to store sugar and not brought to the table → tevila without a brocha.

items.name: Tablecloth / Napkins
items.notes: Tablecloths and napkins do not require tevila.

items.name: Taps / Spigots (on barrels)
items.notes: Taps of barrels require tevila only if the barrel itself requires tevila. Taps of kitchen sinks do not require tevila.

items.name: Teapot (metal or glass)
items.notes: A teapot brought to the table requires tevila with a brocha. Liquid directly contacts the metal or glass interior.

items.name: Teflon-coated Pan
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha. The Teflon coating on the metal changes the brocha status.

items.name: Thermos
items.notes: Metal or glass thermos → tevila with a brocha. Thermos with a plastic casing and removable metal/glass insert → the insert requires tevila with a brocha; the casing does not. Should preferably be immersed assembled.

items.name: Toaster
items.notes: Requires tevila with a brocha. The Teflon-coated rack that contacts food must be immersed.
items.debates: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 3:24) held a toaster is exempt because bread is already edible before entering, making it a question whether it qualifies as a keili seudah. CRC (Rav Schwartz) rules electrical appliances that would be ruined by immersion are exempt. STAR-K rules tevila without a brocha for Teflon-coated surfaces. Many poskim disagree with Rav Moshe and require tevila with a brocha.

items.name: Toaster Oven
items.notes: The rack and tray require tevila with a brocha if food is placed directly on them. The heating element and chamber do not require tevila. If it will break from immersion, ask a Rav.

items.name: Tongs (serving / food)
items.notes: Tongs used for sugar, ice cubes, or serving food. Food contacts the metal directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

items.name: Trivet
items.notes: No tevila if food does not contact the surface. Pots are placed on the trivet.

items.name: Vegetable / Potato Masher
items.notes: Used for mashing cooked potatoes and other vegetables. Since it contacts ready-to-eat food, tevila with a brocha is required.

items.name: Waffle Maker
items.notes: Tevila without a brocha because the metal cooking surfaces are Teflon-coated. If toveling will break it, consult a Rav.

items.name: Warming Tray
items.notes: Food does not contact the surface directly. No tevila required.

items.name: Washing Cup / Netilas Yadayim Cup (metal)
items.notes: If used only for netilas yadayim (hand-washing), no tevila is required. It is not a keili seudah.

items.name: Water Cooler / Dispenser
items.notes: If completely plastic except for internal metal cooling pipes, debated whether tevila is required. If the metal pipe contacts the water that is dispensed for drinking, many require tevila without a brocha. Consult a Rav.

items.name: Water Tank / Solar Boiler
items.notes: Water tanks and solar boilers do not require tevila.

items.name: Wicker Utensils
items.notes: Wicker is a type of wood. Wicker utensils do not require tevila.

items.name: Wooden Cask / Barrel
items.notes: Plain wood → no tevila. If it has metal straps/bands → tevila without a brocha.
